scope: External creator revenue linked to YouTube, not direct platform payout and not total creator income.

datasets.title: Rich-get-richer? Platform attention and earnings inequality using Patreon earnings data
datasets.youtube_relation: Creators with Patreon income and only one declared social-platform affiliation, YouTube
datasets.geography: Not restricted to an identified country in the published table
datasets.threshold: Monthly Patreon earnings greater than USD 10; zero and small earners excluded
datasets.sampling: Patreon monthly earnings dataset purchased directly from Patreon. Authors filter to Patreon accounts affiliated with only one social platform. Missing earnings imputed with a regression model.
limitations: The sample does not represent all YouTube creators and excludes non-Patreon and zero/low Patreon earners.
Patreon earnings are not YouTube native advertising, Premium, memberships, sponsorships or total creator income.
Some creator earnings are model-imputed; unusually successful creators are more likely to conceal figures.
Pooled monthly observations over three March periods are not a current-month income forecast.
Creators affiliated with more than one external social platform were excluded.
These earnings omit production costs, so they are not creator profit.
datasets.recommended_use: Illustrate the degree of dispersion and selection bias in off-platform patron income, not estimate typical YouTube earnings.
